Sea surface temperature—the temperature of the water at the ocean surface—is an important physical attribute of the world’s oceans. As EPA’s Sea Surface Temperature indicator explains, sea surface temperature increases as the oceans absorb more heat, and the ocean circulation patterns that transport warm and cold water around the globe change. Rising sea surface temperatures can disrupt marine ecosystems, affect people who depend on income from fishing or coastal tourism, and raise the risk of seafood contamination. Sea surface temperatures also affect weather patterns, as warmer water leads to more evaporation that feeds stronger storm systems.
